method: Written from the Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022 (SOR/2022-105) Schedule 3 BEFORE running any of them. Each case quotes the row it was read from. Points are point-on-surface interior points of the named provincial units, taken from the certified registry, so the federal area is resolved the way a hunt resolves it rather than asserted.

cases.law: Schedule 3 Part 2 Table 1 item 1(f): 'Snipe | 20 | October 1 to December 31 | 10'. November 5 is inside.
Same row. July 4 is outside October 1 to December 31, and no other Part 2 row opens Snipe, so it is CLOSED rather than unknown.

Item 1(b): 'Ducks (other than Harlequin Ducks, Common and Red-breasted Mergansers, Long-tailed Ducks, Eiders and Scoters), combined | 18 (not more than 1 may be Barrow's Goldeneye) | October 1 to January 15 | 6 (not more than 1 may be Barrow's Goldeneye)'. Mallard is in that group; the limit is the GROUP's.
Same row. October 1 to January 15 runs over the new year, so January 10 is inside it.
Same row. September 15 is before October 1 and after January 15, so outside the season on both ends.

Item 1(d): 'all Geese, combined' carries a bag that CHANGES inside the season — '(A) 5 (from October 1 to November 14)', '(B) 3 (from November 15 to December 31)' — and a September row with 'plus an additional 5 Canada Geese or Cackling Geese'. North Ground refuses rows it cannot state exactly, so this is UNKNOWN naming the refusal, never a guessed number.

Schedule 3 Part 9: 'Zone No. 1 means Provincial Wildlife Management Units 200, ...'. Table 1 Zone No. 1: 'Canada Geese, Cackling Geese and White-fronted Geese, combined | September 1 to December 16 | 8'.
Same row. Zone No. 1 opens September 1, so September 3 is inside.

'Zone No. 2 means Provincial Wildlife Management Units 102, ...' and its geese season is 'September 8 to December 23'. September 3 is before it. The two zones differ by a week, which is the whole reason the federal area must be resolved from the PROVINCIAL unit.
Zone No. 2 runs to December 23, where Zone No. 1 ended December 16.

Alberta's duck rows carry possession '(i) 24 for residents of Canada' and '(ii) 24 (not more than 6 may be Barrow's Goldeneye or Common Goldeneye in any combination) for non-residents of Canada'. A limit that varies by residency cannot be stated for an unknown hunter, so the row is refused and the answer is UNKNOWN — not CLOSED, because the season exists.

Schedule 3 Part 9 names neither 728 nor 730 in Zone No. 1 or Zone No. 2. The regulation places this certified provincial unit in no federal area, so North Ground holds no federal season for it and must not assume it into a neighbour.
Part 12: 'Southern Yukon means the portion of Yukon lying south of latitude 62 degrees N'. Table 1 Southern Yukon: 'all Ducks, combined | September 1 to October 31 | 8'.
Southern Yukon has no August row at all, so December is outside every season encoded or refused, and CLOSED is the honest answer.

Central Yukon ducks: '(i) August 15 to August 31, for residents of Yukon only'. That season EXISTS for a Yukon resident, so CLOSED would state a restriction stricter than the law. North Ground answers UNKNOWN and quotes the refused row.
Northern Yukon: 'Sandhill Cranes | N/A | No open season | N/A'. A declared closure is the authority saying there is no season, which is CLOSED and not UNKNOWN.
Central Yukon: 'Sandhill Cranes | (ii) September 1 to October 31 | 2'. The same species is closed one band north and open here, which is what makes the band resolution load-bearing.
